subject: Obtaining a Custom HTML Input's Current Value

messages.author: 7b36a5521b8eb4d4
messages.subject: Obtaining a Custom HTML Input's Current Value
parts: If the input element is not a Shiny-provided one, but a user-created one, and it is not meant to be reactive, how may its value be accessed in server.R ? This enquiry is similar to an unanswered one on an RStudio blog post. The use case is a complicated input area followed by a Submit button. Only the button is reactive, so I don't think that turning the input into a widget and using bindings should be necessary.

messages.author: a5edeb4fa89b826c
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining a Custom HTML Input's Current Value
parts:
On Friday, June 3, 2016 at 2:00:07 AM UTC-4, Dario Strbenac wrote:
If the input element is not a Shiny-provided one, but a user-created one, and it is not meant to be reactive, how may its value be accessed in server.R ? This enquiry is similar to an unanswered one on an RStudio blog post. The use case is a complicated input area followed by a Submit button. Only the button is reactive, so I don't think that turning the input into a widget and using bindings should be necessary.

There's probably a better solution than this and I hesitate to even mention it as I've never tried something like this myself and don't know if it's a good idea, but it is possible to access HTTP POST values in a Shiny app.  So, if the values from your complicated input area were to be posted as from a regular HTML form, you could access those name and value pairs by reading from session$request$rook.input .  There is a somewhat-relevant example of doing this here:  http://www.asktop2.com/questions/931563/accept-http-request-in-r-shiny-application 

Joel
